Work with the columns of a wgh_data object

Source: R/core-data.R
wgh_data_access.Rd

A wgh_data object holds the standardised data ($data), the column mapping ($map) and the data checks ($log). For convenience it also behaves like its data: x$age returns a column, x$bmi <- ... adds or replaces one, x[rows, ] keeps the selected rows and returns a wgh_data (mapping and checks kept, rows where a logical condition is NA dropped), x[rows, cols] returns a tibble, and nrow(x), ncol(x) and dim(x) refer to the data. The names data, map and log always refer to the parts of the object, so a data column with one of these names must be reached through x$data.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'wgh_data'
x$name

# S3 method for class 'wgh_data'
x$name <- value

# S3 method for class 'wgh_data'
x[i, j, ..., drop = FALSE]

# S3 method for class 'wgh_data'
dim(x)

Arguments

x

A wgh_data object.

name

A column name, or data, map or log.

value

New values.

i, j

Row and column indices, as for a data frame.

...

Not used.

drop

Passed to the tibble when columns are selected.

Value

See Description.

Examples

gd <- wgh_data(growdat, id = "pid", sex = "sex", age = "age", height = "height", weight = "weight")
summary(gd$age)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   1.500   5.197   8.509   8.969  12.505  18.494 
older <- gd[gd$age >= 10, ]
older
#> <wgh_data>: 3425 visits from 1669 children
#> Ages 10 to 18.49 years. Sex: Male 1812, Female 1613
#> Sites: Site1, Site2, Site3
#> Mapping: id = pid, age = age, sex = sex, height = height, weight = weight
nrow(older)
#> [1] 3425
head(gd[, c("id", "age", "height")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   id        age height
#>   <chr>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 C000001  3.00    95 
#> 2 C000001  3.90   103.
#> 3 C000001  6.13   117.
#> 4 C000001  7.10   123.
#> 5 C000001  8.09   129.
#> 6 C000001  9.00   134.
